title: The Leader Who Won't Step Down

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE V: FAMILY DRAMA, FEUDS AND LEADERSHIP DISPUTES (LCE-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
All sorts of real-life drama suited to Isola: parents with opinions about who their children marry, arranged matches, inheritances, feuds between families, accusations, apologies that are not enough, and arguments about who should lead.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The leader is old and tired but refuses to step down: press them, or support them until they are ready.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The {@chief} is very old now, forgets things, and falls asleep at meetings. (subject) thinks it is time for a new {@chief} and wants to say so. (friend) thinks it would break the old {@chief}'s heart. The village is beginning to struggle. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) goes to the {@chief}, privately, and says it as gently as (subject.he/she) can. The {@chief} is quiet for a long time, and then cries, and then agrees. At the next gathering, (other.he/she) steps down with great dignity. (subject) feels terrible and right at the same time.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village quietly takes on more of the {@chief}'s work: others run the meetings, the {@chief} blesses the decisions. It works for a while. Then the {@chief}, seeing it, steps down on (other.his/her) own. (other.He/she) thanks the village for letting (other.him/her) choose.
